thread.title: Apple Will Be Fine but the Best Returns Will Be Elsewhere

title: Apple Will Be Fine but the Best Returns Will Be Elsewhere
text:
Apple Will Be Fine but the Best Returns Will Be Elsewhere By aapl
The Apple ( AAPL ) earnings report tonight is extremely important because it has the largest market capitalization of any stock in the market and has long been a favorite of many money managers and investors. It is an 800 pound gorilla and will move the indices.
I don't typically bet on a response to earnings but I believe it is likely that Action Alerts PLUS holding Apple will see a positive response to its report. Others seem to think the same thing which is why it is trading up today despite the fact that many folks are anticipating that it may have a disappointing quarter and may cut guidance due to slow iPhone X sales and increased competition in Asia.
Apple will be announcing plans to return some of its substantial cash horde to shareholders. That is likely to take the form of stock buy-backs that will help to keep a bid under the stock.
Should you own Apple? It depends on your investing style.
Apple has a very strong balance sheet and buybacks are going to give it a very good cushion. It is not an unreasonably expensive stock. It trades with a trailing PE of just 17 and eps growth for the year is currently expected to be 23%. That may come down and it still won't be very expensive.
Apple, under Steve Jobs, used to be the master of the estimate lowball. That is what made it such an exciting stock to own for many years. It is now a safe haven stock. You can park some cash there and be fairly comfortable that it will be safe. It still has its cult following and there are many people that are emotionally attached to the stock after owning it for so long. It is an old friend and that will help to provide support as well.
I have no interest in owning Apple at this point. I am confident I can find many other stocks that will perform much better. As a trader I'm not worried about parking cash in a safe haven. The safest place to be in a poor market is cash and I prefer that to Apple in the current environment.
It will be very interesting to see what happens with Apple tonight. I don't recall them every having a really poor earnings report and when they have been conservative in the guidance it still attracts buyers.
Whatever happens with Apple tonight it will be a market positive to have it out of the way so that there is a greater focus on the stocks that are working and have strong short term growth. Apple will likely be fine, but it is not the stock to look to if you are looking to produce superior returns. Get an email alert each time I write an article for Real Money.
